name: Learn manual camera controls
blurb: Aperture, shutter speed and ISO — the exposure triangle. Once you understand what each one costs you, manual mode stops being intimidating and starts being useful.
gear: A tripod for the slow-shutter exercises
steps: Learn what each control does and what it costs: aperture controls depth of field, shutter speed controls motion blur, ISO controls noise.
Shoot in aperture priority for a week, deliberately using both f/1.8 and f/11 and comparing the depth of field.
Shoot in shutter priority for a week: freeze motion at 1/1000, blur it deliberately at 1/15.
Learn the reciprocal rule for handholding, and when a tripod is genuinely necessary.
Learn to read the histogram rather than trusting the rear screen, and learn exposure compensation.
Shoot a full session in manual, setting all three yourself, and review what you got wrong.
tips: Auto ISO with manual aperture and shutter is a legitimate and very practical middle ground.
Blown highlights cannot be recovered; shadows often can. When in doubt, expose for the highlights.
proof: You shoot a whole session in manual and nail exposure in changing light without chimping every frame.
